does: Whisks cold butter into a hot liquid off the boil, so that it melts into a smooth, glossy, lightly thickened sauce and not into a layer of fat.

intro.what: Mounting with butter brings cold butter into a reduced hot liquid away from the boil.
intro.why: It teaches you to build gloss and light thickness while keeping the butter from separating into oil.

how: Boil the liquid down first, until only a few syrupy, strong spoonfuls are left in the pan.
Take the pan off the heat, or turn the heat to its lowest.
Add cold butter in small cubes, a few at a time, and whisk or swirl the pan until each lot has vanished before the next goes in.
Stop when the sauce is glossy and coats a spoon. Season it and serve it at once: it can be neither boiled nor kept.

cues.text: The sauce turns opaque, glossy and creamy, with no beads of clear fat at the edge.
It coats a spoon lightly, like thin cream.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the butter over high heat, or letting the sauce boil afterwards, which melts the butter to oil and leaves the sauce greasy.
mistakes.fix: Take the pan off the heat. If the sauce splits, whisk in a spoonful of cold water or cream off the heat.

mistakes.mistake: Using soft or melted butter, which goes straight to oil.
mistakes.fix: Use butter cold from the fridge, cut small.

mistakes.mistake: Too much liquid left in the pan, so that the butter cannot thicken it.
mistakes.fix: Reduce further before the butter goes in.

quiz.question: What finish is this method intended to give a sauce?
choices: A clear layer of fat on top.
A thinner sauce with visible pools of butter.
A smooth, glossy, lightly thickened finish.
quiz.because: Butter held in the sauce gives a smooth, glossy finish. Separate pools of fat mean it has split.

quiz.question: How is the butter added in this method?
choices: Cold and in small additions, whisking or swirling each in.
Melted and poured in all at once over high heat.
Soft and left unstirred on a rolling boil.
quiz.because: Small additions of cold butter, whisked in away from the boil, help it join the sauce rather than melt into a separate layer.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches the intended sauce?
choices: Clear fat beads around a thin centre.
An opaque, glossy sauce without clear fat at the edge.
A separate pool of melted butter.
quiz.because: An opaque, glossy sauce without clear fat at the edge shows the finish this method aims for.

quiz.question: The sauce splits after getting too hot. What could help bring it together?
choices: Boil harder to drive off the fat.
Add more melted butter over high heat.
Take it off the heat and whisk in a little cold water or cream.
quiz.because: Excess heat can split the sauce. Take it off the heat; whisking in a little cold water or cream may help bring it together.

comes_after.why: Butter can only be mounted into a liquid that has been boiled down first.

variant_of.differs: The fat is cold butter, the liquid is hot, and nothing but the butter's own milk solids holds the sauce together.
